*   When `include_environment_context` is `false`, the client must not include any `<environment_context>` tag or its contents in user-role messages sent to the API — this must be observable in the request body's input field

## Changes

**`codex-rs/core/src/config/profile.rs`**
- Added `pub include_environment_context: Option<bool>` to `ConfigProfile` for profile-level overrides.

**`codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs`**
- Added `pub include_environment_context: bool` to the `Config` struct.
- Added `pub include_environment_context: Option<bool>` to the `ConfigToml` struct.
- Added resolution logic following the existing pattern: profile value takes precedence over the top-level config value, defaulting to `true` when both are absent:
  ```rust
  let include_environment_context = config_profile
      .include_environment_context
      .or(cfg.include_environment_context)
      .unwrap_or(true);
  ```
- Wired it into the `Config` construction.

**`codex-rs/core/src/codex.rs`** (`build_initial_context`)
- Gated the `<environment_context>` push into `contextual_user_sections` behind `if turn_context.config.include_environment_context`, so it's omitted entirely from the initial user message when disabled.

**`codex-rs/core/src/context_manager/updates.rs`** (`build_environment_update_item`)
- Added an early `return None` when `!next.config.include_environment_context`, so turn-to-turn environment diffs are also suppressed (mirroring the existing `build_permissions_update_item` guard).

**`codex-rs/core/src/config/config_tests.rs`**
- Updated the four existing `Config` struct literals with `include_environment_context: true` so the existing test module keeps compiling (this is a `#[cfg(test)]` module under `src/`, not the `tests/` directory).

When `include_environment_context` is `false`, no `<environment_context>` tag or content is emitted into any user-role message, observable in the request body's `input` field. Existing behavior is preserved by the `true` default in both the config-loading path and the on-disk `ConfigToml`/`ConfigProfile` resolution.
